premise.claim: When a RoleBasedGroupSet / RoleBasedGroup is deleted and recreated with the same name, the new object gets a new UID while the predecessor's children linger until GC: the recreated Set listed children purely by the set-name label (could delete a foreign child on scale-down, rewrite its spec, count it Ready in status); the RBG controller read a bound ScalingAdapter by name (a leftover adapter could pin a stale replica count); both gang PodGroup implementations reused the PodGroup found by name and rewrote its spec while keeping the old controller reference, and the Volcano path never adopted orphans.
premise.reportedComponent: RoleBasedGroupSet controller, RoleBasedGroup controller (scaling-adapter paths), pkg/scheduler/k8s-scheduler-plugin, pkg/scheduler/volcano
premise.evidence: All five P0 contract tests FAIL on base 56c4953 (foreign child deleted on scale-down; ReadyReplicas counted 1; role replicas 3 pinned to 9; both foreign PodGroup specs rewritten 1->2 with no error) and PASS on head d2915172. Raw output: results/base-56c4953-premise.json, results/head-d2915172.json

integration._note: controller-runtime envtest against a real API server; assets per machine via 'go run sigs.k8s.io/controller-runtime/tools/setup-envtest@release-0.22 use 1.31.0 --bin-dir /tmp/envtest-bin -p path'. Not tied to any single finding; general no-regression gate for the controller changes.

findings._note: Regression suite for the PR's own fix (the P0 tests re-run on every future head). Must keep passing; a flip means the ownership fix regressed.

Open finding: orphaned PodGroup whose spec already matches is never adopted, so deletePodGroup's IsControlledBy gate leaks it. Proposed fix validated in the harness-bites check: add '|| !metav1.IsControlledBy(podGroup, rbg)' to the spec-drift condition in both schedulers; with that patch both tests pass and the full pkg/scheduler/... suite stays green.
